The Ca-EDTA complex dissociates according to the equilibrium:

\[ \text{CaY}^{2-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{Y}^{4-} \]

The formation constant is given by:

\[ K_f = \frac{[\text{CaY}^{2-}]}{[\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{Y}^{4-}]} = 5 \times 10^{10} \]

Initially, the stoichiometric concentration of the complex is 0.02 M. Let \( x \) be the concentration of free \( \text{Ca}^{2+} \) and \( \text{Y}^{4-} \) at equilibrium. Then:

\[ [\text{CaY}^{2-}] = 0.02 - x \approx 0.02 \]
\[ [\text{Ca}^{2+}] = x \]
\[ [\text{Y}^{4-}] = x \]

Substituting into the expression for \( K_f \):

\[ 5 \times 10^{10} = \frac{0.02}{x^2} \]
\[ x^2 = \frac{0.02}{5 \times 10^{10}} = 4 \times 10^{-13} \]
\[ x = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-13}} = 2 \times 10^{-6.5} \approx 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{M} \]

Thus, the concentration of calcium ions is \( 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{M} \).

Answer: D
